She prepares two calculations: Michigan’s ten business days and the federal fourteen calendar days. If delivery evidence or the treatment of a holiday remains unresolved, the planned acceptance date stays pending. A current annual notice does not repair an insufficient disclosure period.

sections.heading: Keep a transaction record beside the annual calendar
bullets: Retain the filed notice, filing date and one-year anniversary.
Save the delivered FDD, Michigan page and all proposed agreements.
Record the recipient and evidence of delivery.
Show business-day and calendar-day calculations separately against the earlier relevant event.
Record subsequent agreement changes and who initiated them for any additional review.

practicalOutput: A Michigan annual-notice record and a sale-specific schedule showing the required documents, delivery evidence and separate state and federal timing calculations.
limitations: The guide does not decide a particular fee exclusion, exemption or complete ongoing-contract question. The recorded full current definition and prohibited-provision statute routes were blocked; the definition described here is the agency’s quoted definition.
Actual parties, offer locations and dates need application review. Tax, employment, sector rules, operating permits and address-dependent requirements remain separate from filing and disclosure.

title: Michigan disclosure timing: check business days and calendar days separately
description: Use the actual document delivery, agreement and payment events to calculate both applicable waiting periods.
learningSummary: A prospective operator needs time to read the sales documents before becoming committed. Michigan and federal law measure that time differently. A sales coordinator should prepare two calculations, using the correct documents and actual delivery facts, before scheduling a signature or accepting a deposit.

keyTerms.meaning: Giving the prospective buyer the required information and documents before the relevant commitment.
Payment or other value relevant to the statutory trigger.
An agreement creating a legal commitment.
Days counted on the calendar, including weekends.
Days counted under the applicable business-day rule; holiday treatment must be checked rather than guessed.

sections.heading: Start with Michigan’s earlier event
paragraphs: Michigan section 445.1508 calls for the disclosure statement, prescribed Michigan notice and proposed agreements at least ten business days before a binding agreement or consideration, whichever occurs first. Include the required state page and every proposed agreement in the delivery record.

Identify both the planned signing and any earlier payment or other relevant consideration. A deposit should not disappear from the timetable merely because the main agreement will be signed later. The legal treatment of the actual event must be established before the team relies on the proposed date.

sections.heading: Make a second, federal calculation
paragraphs: The federal Franchise Rule has its independent 14-calendar-day disclosure requirement where it applies. The Michigan calculation does not replace it, and the federal calculation does not replace the state’s business-day requirement.

Do not convert ten business days into a fixed number of calendar days. The result depends on the actual dates and the applicable treatment of holidays. Compare both calculations against their relevant triggers and documents. This worksheet does not decide that an exemption applies under either system.

sections.heading: Fictional example: a Singapore service brand near a holiday
paragraphs: A Singapore brand delivers documents shortly before a holiday period and plans to take a partner deposit two weeks later. The coordinator records the actual delivery method, recipient and delivery or receipt facts. She lists the deposit and signature as separate proposed events.

She then counts the federal calendar days and separately checks the Michigan business days. “Two weeks” is a description of the plan, not proof that both legal periods have run. If the treatment of a holiday or the legally relevant delivery date remains uncertain, the team must resolve that question before relying on the planned payment date. A later signature does not automatically fix an earlier payment problem.

sections.heading: Use a worksheet that shows the inputs
paragraphs: Someone reviewing the calculation should be able to see the documents, dates and assumptions without asking the salesperson to reconstruct the conversation. Keep the delivery record with the actual versions, including later changes.

rows: Document version, recipient, delivery method and relevant delivery or receipt facts
Evidence that the required state page was included
Every proposed agreement and a record of subsequent changes
Calendar-day calculation, start event and proposed commitment event
Business-day method and review of relevant holidays
Planned signature, payment and any other relevant consideration

sections.heading: Name uncertainty instead of hiding it
paragraphs: The worksheet does not automatically determine a legal delivery date or apply holiday rules. An unresolved receipt, amendment or negotiation fact remains a question for the responsible reviewer. Do not replace it with a general message that the transaction is ready.

The coordinator’s concrete next step is to obtain the missing delivery evidence or clarify the changed agreement, update both calculations and retain the reason for the eventual date. That produces a usable sale record while keeping separate registration, exemption and other legal questions visible.

practicalOutput: A Michigan disclosure worksheet showing the documents delivered, relevant delivery facts, earliest proposed commitment and separate state business-day and federal calendar-day calculations.
limitations: This worksheet does not determine legal delivery, holiday treatment, the effect of agreement changes or transaction-specific exemptions. Unresolved facts must be reviewed before a commitment date is used.

The timing review does not complete state notice filing, advertising or relationship analysis. Corporate tax, employment, sector requirements, operating permits and actual-address rules remain separate.

title: Minnesota: plan registration, buyer documents and usable support cash
description: An effective filing and an initial franchise fee do not necessarily mean the seller can start spending that fee on support.
learningSummary: A brand entering Minnesota must plan both the legal sales timetable and the money needed to deliver its promises. A financial-assurance condition can restrict when an initial fee is available. The finance and sales teams therefore need the actual registration order, disclosure dates and support costs in one coordinated plan.

keyTerms.meaning: A shared commercial interest examined under Minnesota’s particular franchise definition.
Protection required in the actual financial review to support the seller’s ability to meet its obligations.
An arrangement that holds funds subject to specified conditions rather than leaving them freely available to the seller.
Postponing collection or availability of a fee under the applicable condition.
A guarantee from a surety company under the specified terms.
The state-law term for the current information document required for the prospective buyer.

sections.heading: Apply Minnesota’s own definition
paragraphs: Current section 80C.01, subdivision 4 includes a route involving brand rights, a community of interest and a direct or indirect fee. It also contains other branches concerning fuel, specified business-opportunity promises and certain security-system payments. The federal control-or-assistance test is not a substitute for this state wording.

Prepare a factsheet of the rights, brand use, shared marketing interest, goods, services, training and required initial or recurring payments. Examine area-franchise scope, fee definitions, exclusions and any claimed wholesale or fair-market-value payment treatment separately. This review identifies the questions; it does not determine that the actual arrangement is covered or exempt.

sections.heading: Use the effective registration order
paragraphs: Section 80C.02 requires an effective registration before a covered offer or sale unless the franchise or transaction is exempt under section 80C.03. The Department directs electronic filings through ComOnline. A prepared application is not the same as an effective registration.

Under section 80C.08, the registration is effective for 12 months from the Commissioner’s order, and the prescribed annual report must be filed before that period ends. Retain the order and actual end date. Renewing a registration is a different matter from renewing an existing operator’s contract.

sections.heading: Check when initial fees can actually be used
paragraphs: The financial-assurance guidance says the Commissioner may require escrow, impoundment or deferral where adequate financial arrangements have not been demonstrated. It describes a surety-bond alternative and deferral of initial franchise fees until the franchisee has opened.

These are possible conditions in the actual review, not restrictions automatically imposed on every applicant. Read the selected condition and release requirements. Money expected at signature may not be available when the seller needs to pay trainers or travel costs. Recording fee revenue in accounts does not establish spendable cash.

sections.heading: Fictional example: a German maintenance brand funds training
paragraphs: A German maintenance brand expects an initial fee at signature to pay a trainer and opening visits. Suppose its actual condition defers that fee until the operator opens. The training and travel must occur earlier, so the fee cannot fund those earlier costs under that condition.

The finance director lists the payment dates and identifies committed capital available during the gap. If a different assurance applies, the calculation must use its actual terms instead. The useful result is a dated cash plan explaining how support will be delivered, rather than an assumption that every signed sale brings immediately usable funds.

sections.heading: Give the buyer documents under both applicable rules
paragraphs: The agency’s seven-day wording matches current 2026 section 80C.06, subdivision 5. For a franchise subject to state registration requirements, provide the current public offering statement and all proposed agreements at least seven days before the earlier of execution of any franchise or other agreement or payment of consideration. Consideration means the relevant payment or other value.

Obtain a signed acknowledgement before agreement or payment and retain it for three years from taking it. The independent federal 14-calendar-day disclosure requirement remains applicable where its coverage requires it. Seven state-law days do not shorten that federal period. Keep the documents, triggers, delivery and acknowledgement dates separately.

sections.heading: Keep existing-operator decisions separate
paragraphs: The separate Minnesota relationship guide addresses section 80C.14’s termination, nonrenewal and transfer branches. A valid annual registration does not itself approve ending a contract, refusing to renew it or rejecting a transfer.

The company secretary and finance director should finish this sales plan together: registration order and annual report dates; buyer documents and receipt retention; initial support costs; available committed funds; and the selected assurance and release evidence. Any exemption or financial condition must be tied to the actual transaction and order.

practicalOutput: A Minnesota plan showing effective registration and reporting dates, buyer-document delivery and receipt retention, and how support is funded before any restricted fee becomes available.
limitations: No transaction, fee exclusion, sector exception or exemption is determined here. Assurance and release requirements depend on the actual financial review and terms, not a universal cash threshold.

Agreement changes and delivery facts need their own review. Contract renewal, termination and transfer, corporate tax, employment, operating permits and address-specific requirements remain separate decisions.

title: Minnesota: choose the right rule before ending or changing an operator’s agreement
description: Termination, nonrenewal and transfer each have different cause, notice and evidence questions.
learningSummary: An operator’s agreement may end because the brand terminates it early, refuses a new term or responds to a proposed sale of the business. Those are different decisions under Minnesota law. Management should identify the actual action and purpose before choosing a notice period or sending a letter.

keyTerms.meaning: The legally sufficient reason required by the applicable provision; a contract label does not establish it.
Correcting the specified failure within the applicable opportunity to do so.
Refusing to continue the relationship into a further term when the existing term ends.
A business valued as a continuing operation, rather than only its separate assets or initial fee.
A proposed change of ownership or operator requiring the relevant consent review.
The business value associated with reputation and customer relationships.

sections.heading: Define the covered relationship and actual action
paragraphs: Start with section 80C.01’s franchise definition and the recognized-classification context in section 80C.14, subdivisions 1–2. Do not assume one rule applies to every commercial or sector arrangement. Then describe whether management proposes termination or cancellation, failure to renew, or withholding consent to a transfer.

Registration expiry and contract expiry are separate events. A filing calendar does not decide whether ending the operator’s agreement is lawful. Keep the contract term, actual conduct and intended result in the decision file.

sections.heading: For termination, examine cause and notice separately
paragraphs: Subdivision 3 requires good cause. It states a 90-day written notice containing all reasons and 60 days from receipt to correct the failure, subject to separate immediate-effect exceptions. Preserve whether the requirement was material and reasonable, what failed, the reasons stated, actual receipt and the correction history.

The immediate-effect exceptions concern specified abandonment, a business-related conviction and the prescribed uncured goodwill-default branch. A fact listed as good cause does not automatically appear in the immediate-notice exception list. The goodwill branch itself requires the prescribed prior cure notice. A clause allowing immediate termination for breach does not establish those statutory facts.

sections.heading: For nonrenewal, use the separate statutory branches
paragraphs: Subdivision 4 separately addresses good-cause and failure-to-correct cases. It also has a route requiring at least 180 days’ advance notice plus the stated opportunity to operate long enough to recover fair market value as a going concern, measured from the failure to renew.

Do not translate that language into an automatic cash refund, a guaranteed compensation payment or repayment of the initial fee. It requires examination of the statutory operating opportunity and value. The provision also prohibits refusing renewal for the purpose of converting the franchisee’s premises to the franchisor’s own operation. Record the real business plan, not merely the letter’s chosen heading.

sections.heading: For transfer, compare the proposed buyer with current standards
paragraphs: Subdivision 5 addresses unreasonably withholding consent where the replacement meets the franchisor’s present qualifications and standards. Collect those current standards and the proposed buyer’s evidence, then record the actual reasons for the decision.

This is not a rule requiring approval of every transfer. Nor should an unsupported statement that a buyer is unsuitable replace comparison with the present qualifications and standards. The practical task is a documented decision on the actual proposed replacement.

sections.heading: Fictional example: weak performance as the term ends
paragraphs: A service brand is unhappy with an operator’s results. The agreement is nearing expiry, and management wants to run the same premises itself. Calling the proposed action “nonrenewal” does not remove the need to examine that purpose, the statutory nonrenewal conditions and the prohibition concerning conversion to the brand’s own operation.

The reviewer also separates any claimed performance failure from the notice and cure history. If management considers early termination instead, the good-cause requirement and the correct notice branch need their own analysis. The exercise produces questions and a factual record; it does not establish good cause, going-concern value or permission for either outcome.

sections.heading: Prepare one decision file for the actual action
bullets: Explain the covered relationship and any relevant classification or rule.
State the proposed conduct and commercial purpose: early exit, nonrenewal or transfer decision.
Keep cause evidence separate from any immediate-effect exception relied on.
Retain notices, stated reasons, receipt evidence, correction steps and contract expiry.
For nonrenewal, preserve the operating-opportunity and going-concern evidence.
For transfer, attach present standards, buyer qualifications and the actual reasons.

practicalOutput: A Minnesota decision file separating the proposed action, cause, notice and correction dates, nonrenewal purpose and operating opportunity, or transfer qualifications and reasons.
limitations: This guide addresses section 80C.14 within its franchise and classification scope. It approves no termination, nonrenewal, transfer or monetary recovery.
No going-concern valuation or complete Commissioner-rule, sector, bankruptcy or judicial analysis is supplied. Other contract, federal, state and local duties remain separate.

title: Minnesota support funding: check when the initial fee becomes usable cash
description: Use the actual financial-assurance condition to identify how pre-opening training and other support will be paid for.
learningSummary: A seller may owe training and opening support before it can use an initial franchise fee. Minnesota’s financial review can produce conditions affecting that timing. The finance director needs a month-by-month cash plan using the actual condition, rather than assuming that a signed sale pays for everything that follows.

keyTerms.meaning: Protection required under the actual review when adequate financial arrangements have not been demonstrated.
Holding money under conditions that restrict when it can be released or used.
A financial guarantee from a surety company under the specified terms.
Postponing the fee under the applicable arrangement, such as until the operator opens.
The amount needed to pay costs before committed, usable receipts are available.

sections.heading: Read the actual condition before modelling the fee
paragraphs: Minnesota’s published guidance describes escrow, impoundment, a surety-bond alternative and fee-deferral arrangements where financial assurance is required. Where adequate financial arrangements have not been demonstrated, the Commissioner may impose the applicable protection. This is not a finding that every applicant faces the same condition.

If the actual arrangement delays receipt or release until opening or another event, the fee is unavailable for earlier cash costs unless another source covers the gap. Read the order, agreement and release requirements together. Do not substitute an assumed cash threshold or a standard model from a different applicant.

sections.heading: List support costs by payment date
paragraphs: Training wages, travel and other promised opening support can fall due before the operator starts trading. Put each actual obligation into the month when cash must be paid. Then identify committed receipts that can legally and practically be used in that same period.

An expected fee and an available bank balance are different inputs. Revenue recognised in accounts also does not by itself pay a bill. The planning question is whether spendable money is available before the particular obligation falls due.

sections.heading: Fictional example: costs in month one, fee in month three
paragraphs: Assume solely for planning that a brand must pay $12,000 for training travel and wages in month one, while its initial fee becomes available in month three. The pre-opening funding calculation starts with that dated $12,000 outflow plus any other actual outflows. Reduce it only by committed receipts usable in those months.

If the month-three fee is the only expected receipt, it cannot pay a month-one bill on time. The business needs separate available capital for the earlier period. Once that funding is identified, record its amount, availability, cost and constraints. Do not count both the $12,000 expense and an identical arbitrary reserve as two different costs.
The $12,000 is invented for this illustration. It is not a Minnesota fee, minimum capital amount or required reserve. The timing of the actual order and actual costs controls the real plan.

sections.heading: Test a later opening as well
paragraphs: If release depends on opening, a delayed opening can extend the period before the fee becomes usable. Show a reasonable downside opening-date assumption and the actual costs affected by that delay. This is a planning exercise, not a prediction of the examiner’s condition or an instruction to add an unexplained reserve.

Name the person who confirms that the release event has occurred and retains the required evidence. A forecast date is not release evidence. Update the cash plan if the condition or opening timetable changes.

sections.heading: Give finance a short, verifiable file
bullets: Attach the exact financial condition and identify its release trigger.
List support obligations and cash payment dates.
Identify committed cash actually available before release.
Retain alternative-funding evidence, including cost and restrictions.
Assign the release check and retain evidence of the event.
Show the effect of a later opening without duplicating costs.

practicalOutput: A dated funding plan showing how the seller will pay pre-opening support costs before any restricted initial fee becomes available.
limitations: The illustration predicts neither an examiner’s condition nor an approved funding level. Use the actual order or agreement and reviewed guidance; release requirements vary with the selected arrangement.
This cash exercise does not complete registration, disclosure, exemption or agreement-change analysis. Corporate tax, employment, operating permits and actual-address requirements remain separate.

title: Missouri: document territory promises and review exit notice separately
description: Recruitment representations and an existing operator’s exit use different definitions and legal tests.
learningSummary: A brand can face one question when promising a territory and another when ending an operator’s rights. Missouri’s business-opportunity rules address specified sales promises, while its franchise relationship rules have their own coverage and notice requirements. Keep both decisions clear in the commercial documents and management record.

keyTerms.meaning: A shared commercial interest assessed under the particular franchise relationship definition.
A promise that specified rights in an area or market are reserved to an operator; the exact limits must be clear.
A decision not to continue the agreement into a further term.
Business value associated with reputation and customer relationships.
The connection between an alleged legal failure and the loss claimed.
A court remedy directing or preventing conduct, rather than only awarding money.

sections.heading: Identify which relationship is covered before counting notice days
paragraphs: Section 407.400 uses a licence and community-of-interest definition, an in-state place-of-business condition and specific exclusions. Apply those facts before assuming the relationship is covered. The heading on the contract is not the whole test.

For a covered relationship, section 407.405 generally requires at least ninety days’ written notice of cancellation, termination or nonrenewal. There are specified misconduct, abandonment, insolvency and bad-check exceptions. Establish the actual statutory ground and evidence; alleging a default does not automatically establish an exception.

sections.heading: Review recruitment claims under the separate definition
paragraphs: Sections 409.1000 and 409.1003 have their own business-opportunity definition, exclusions and prohibited practices. They address representations about investment, training or support, profits, contract rights and assigning the same so-called exclusive territory to multiple purchasers.

A relationship outside the section 407.400 definition should not automatically be treated as outside this different sales-law definition. For a covered business opportunity, section 409.1003 prohibits failing to provide a written contract and misrepresenting termination, transfer or renewal provisions, alongside the other specified subjects. Compare the proposed agreement with the actual presentation and conversations before commitment.

sections.heading: Fictional example: two territories and national accounts
paragraphs: A Belgian industrial-services brand promises two operators exclusive service territories while retaining national accounts. The operations director draws the geography and records which customers, leads and account types each promise includes. If both operators are told they have exclusive rights to the same customers, the problem cannot be resolved by a map that was never explained in the sales materials.

The director therefore checks the presentations, contract wording and support promises together under the applicable business-opportunity rules. If one operator later misses targets, that is a new decision: the team separately examines section 407.400 coverage, proposed exit, notice and any exception. An accurate original territory statement does not by itself permit immediate termination.

sections.heading: Use the remedy provision for the actual claim
paragraphs: Section 407.410 contains different remedies in different subsections. Subsection 1’s double-consideration and attorney-fee wording concerns inducing participation in a pyramid sales scheme. It must not be imported into an ordinary franchise notice dispute simply because it appears nearby.

Subsection 2 separately permits a franchisee damaged by failure to give required cancellation or termination notice to seek the listed damages, including loss of goodwill, costs and appropriate equitable relief. Keep evidence of coverage, the required notice and failure, causation and actual loss. The provision does not predict an award, and the complete judicial application was not researched here.

sections.heading: Keep a sales file and an exit file
paragraphs: The two files can share the agreement while answering different questions. A sales file records what the buyer was promised. An exit file records why the relationship is being changed and how the applicable notice rule is being addressed.

rows: Exact territory promises, definition analysis and campaign versions
Training and field-support commitments with cost evidence
Agreement, Missouri place-of-business facts, reasons and notice dates
Specific statutory ground and supporting facts
Dealer or professional-sector rules, competition and local activity questions

sections.heading: Assign the next concrete review
paragraphs: Before an offer, have the responsible person compare the territory allocation and promises against the written agreement. Before an exit, have that person identify the relationship coverage and exact notice or exception branch. Neither exercise establishes a universal state FDD period or the absence of a registration requirement.
Preserve unresolved questions in the record instead of treating one narrow conclusion as permission for every part of the transaction. Federal franchise disclosure remains an independent question.

practicalOutput: A Missouri territory-and-promises file plus a separate exit-notice file showing relationship coverage, reasons, the correct exception analysis and any actual loss evidence.
limitations: This guide does not determine the actual model, exemption, notice exception, lawful exit or remedy. Full judicial application, damages and attorney-fee entitlement were not researched, and no award is predicted.
It establishes neither a universal state disclosure period nor absence of registration. Federal, sector-dealer, competition, employment, tax and local requirements need independent review.

title: Montana: check the equipment relationship before changing or ending dealer rights
description: Construction-equipment dealer protections and inventory repurchase rules require separate coverage and evidence checks.
learningSummary: A service brand may add a machine line to its local operator’s business. That can create a separate equipment-dealer question when the supplier later changes targets, competes with the dealer or wants to end the arrangement. Identify the goods and rights first, then examine cause, notice, correction and any inventory repurchase duty.

keyTerms.meaning: The party granting the covered dealership rights, such as the relevant supplier.
The shared commercial interest examined under the construction-equipment dealership definition.
The legally sufficient reason required under the particular dealer provision.
Correcting the identified deficiency within the applicable period.
Buying qualifying stock back under the applicable contract and statutory conditions.

sections.heading: Adding equipment can change the legal questions
paragraphs: Montana’s construction-equipment dealership provisions in part 9 have their own definitions. MCA 30-11-901 includes oral, written, express and implied arrangements and a community of interest in distributing construction equipment. A written service agreement may therefore not be the only relevant evidence.

List the actual equipment, sales and service rights, supplier relationships and communications. Separate retail equipment, wholesale distribution and branded services. This part is not a general definition of a business-format franchise; the equipment and arrangement must fit the particular scope.

sections.heading: Good cause is different from a notice period
paragraphs: Under MCA 30-11-902, a grantor needs good cause for a covered termination, cancellation, nonrenewal or substantial competitive change, and bears the burden of proving it. A substantial competitive change concerns the covered dealer’s competitive circumstances; identify the actual proposed conduct rather than relying on a vague label.

A contract clause or missed sales target does not by itself prove statutory good cause. Retain the requirements, performance facts, treatment of comparable dealers and relevant communications. Even where cause is established, the applicable notice and correction provisions remain a separate question.

sections.heading: Choose the actual notice branch
paragraphs: MCA 30-11-903 generally requires 90 days’ prior notice by certified mail and 60 days to rectify claimed deficiencies. Preserve the notice method, reasons and correction evidence rather than substituting an ordinary email for the specified mailing process.

Nonpayment has a separate 10-day notice and remedy rule. Stated insolvency, assignment-for-creditors and bankruptcy grounds have different notice treatment under subsections (2) and (3). An assignment for creditors is an arrangement concerning assets for the benefit of creditors. Do not apply the ordinary 90/60 timing universally or assume an alleged financial problem satisfies a listed exception.

sections.heading: Fictional example: a maintenance brand adds a machine line
paragraphs: A European maintenance brand authorises its Montana operator to sell a construction machine line alongside branded services. The operator invests in stock and support. Later, the supplier wants to replace it quickly after a missed target.

The operations director first records the equipment, distribution rights and actual relationship to test part 9 coverage. If covered, the supplier needs to address good cause and its proof burden, then select the correct notice and correction branch. The missed target is evidence to assess, not automatic permission for immediate exit. A separate inventory review then asks which stock, if any, qualifies for repurchase.

sections.heading: Value stock under the repurchase rules, not the whole spreadsheet
paragraphs: Part 7 contains a distinct inventory repurchase regime with its own definitions, including industrial and construction equipment and repair parts. Do not assume part 9 coverage automatically decides every part 7 issue.

Review the qualifying contract, inventory condition, price basis and exclusions. Finance should retain stock age, invoices, freight, title and condition records. A spare part appearing on an inventory spreadsheet is not proof that its full listed value is recoverable.

sections.heading: Prepare the proposed-action file before sending notice
bullets: Operations: identify goods, supplier and separate service, retail and wholesale rights.
Finance: retain item-level age, condition, invoice, freight and title evidence.
Relationship manager: record performance requirements, comparable treatment and deficiencies.
Responsible reviewer: select the actual good-cause, notice, correction and repurchase provisions.
Keep general franchise-sales and business-opportunity questions explicitly open until researched.

practicalOutput: A Montana equipment file identifying dealer coverage, the proposed action and cause, the applicable notice and correction branch, and item-level evidence for any repurchase review.
limitations: This guide does not establish coverage, good cause, an exception, an inventory valuation or permission for a particular termination or competitive change. Part 9 and part 7 have separate scopes.

General franchise and business-opportunity sales rules remain unresolved here. Federal disclosure and independent state relationship, sector, tax, employment and local duties need review for the actual parties, places and activities.
